advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish blast-radius glob PATTERNS from ordinary recorded file paths in hash_dep_entry rather than inferring 'glob' from metacharacters, so real filenames containing *, ?, or [ are still content-hashed.
evidence: read_set.py:_GLOB_META = ("*", "?", "[") and is_glob returns True on any occurrence
manifest.py:398 'deps = {p: _read_set.hash_dep_entry(p, base=base) for p in sorted(paths)}' — applied to ALL paths including cited/file_impact, not just blast-radius globs
Prior behavior (diff): 'return {p: _hash_file(p, base=base) for p in sorted(paths)}' hashed every path as content
normalize_read_set existence-filters to real regular files (read_set.py:170), so a real file named e.g. 'x[1].py' can enter the set and be misclassified
advisory.finding: hash_dep_entry classifies any dependency entry containing a glob metacharacter (*, ?, or [) as a glob and computes a membership digest rather than a content hash. Since dependency_hashes now routes EVERY path (cited paths, declared file_impact, normalized read-set paths) through hash_dep_entry, a legitimate real file whose name contains such a character (e.g. 'foo[1].py', a bracketed test fixture) is silently treated as a glob pattern and gets a membership digest instead of its file-content hash — a behavior change from the prior code, which unconditionally used _hash_file for all such paths.
advisory.suggested_fix: Tag blast-radius glob entries explicitly (e.g. a sentinel prefix or a separate entry kind) instead of using is_glob() metacharacter sniffing, so only intended patterns get the membership digest.

evidence: src/rebar/llm/workflow/plan_review_recovery.py:219 `if not normalized:` … `return` (fetches but none survive → no scope)

ABSENCE: `search_files` for `_attach_read_set` and `read_set_recorded` across tests/ returns only the manual assignment inside test_plan_review_attest_drift.py's `_verdict` helper (line 193); no test invokes _attach_read_set
advisory.finding: _attach_read_set (plan_review_recovery.py) — the producer that sets coverage['read_set_recorded'], the load-bearing fail-safe discriminator — has no test. Its three decision branches (no fetch observed → not recorded; fetches observed but none normalize → not recorded; normalization raises → unscoped) are exactly the fail-open/fail-safe boundaries the ADR calls load-bearing, yet the drift tests set read_set_recorded manually via the _verdict helper and never invoke _attach_read_set.
scenarios: A refactor that sets read_set_recorded before checking `if not normalized` would scope reviews whose reads didn't survive normalization (fail-open) — no test fails
A backend reporting zero fetch telemetry incorrectly treated as 'read nothing' → scoping applied on empty observation
